source.title: Object.hasField() returns true for inherited prototype names like toString

labels.name: status:in-linear
labels.description: Issue or PR is now in Linear

source.body:
### Bug Description

`Object.hasField()` uses the `in` operator, so inherited `Object.prototype` names are treated as present fields even when the object has no such own key. That contradicts the docs, which say it "only checks top-level keys".

`({}).hasField('toString')` returns `true`, and so do `constructor` and `hasOwnProperty`. An expression like `{{ $json.hasField('constructor') }}` therefore returns `true` for every item.

### To Reproduce

1. In any node's expression editor, evaluate `{{ ({}).hasField('toString') }}`.
2. Also try `{{ ({}).hasField('constructor') }}` and `{{ ({}).hasField('hasOwnProperty') }}`.
3. All three return `true`.

### Expected behavior

All of the above return `false`, because the object has no such top-level field. `{{ ({ toString: 'custom' }).hasField('toString') }}` should still return `true`.

### Debug Info

Not instance-specific; reproduces on current master in expression evaluation (n8n-workflow object extensions).

### Operating System

Any (Linux tested)

### n8n Version

master (2.x)

### Node.js Version

22

### Database

SQLite (default)

### Execution mode

main (default)

### Hosting

self hosted

comments.author: goutham-valugula
comments.text: One nuance from the current tests: `object-extensions.test.ts` explicitly expects `hasField()` to return true for a key exposed by a Proxy `has`/`get` trap even when there is no own property descriptor. Replacing `in` with `Object.hasOwn()` would make the reported prototype cases false, but would also break that tested Proxy behavior. Is supporting Proxy-exposed fields intentional? If so, an own-property check may need to distinguish ordinary objects from proxies (which JavaScript does not provide a direct general-purpose test for); otherwise the test and docs should be aligned around own keys.
